label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents a sizable group (n=332) of respondents who report consistently low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their UCLA-8 loneliness score averages 1.24, PHQ-9 depression score averages 0.81, and GAD-7 anxiety score averages 0.84—all well below clinical concern thresholds. They appear to be psychologically resilient individuals with stable emotional well-being.

label: High-Distress Heavy-Screen-Use Graduate Women
summary: This profile captures female respondents with graduate-level education or above who spend more than 5 hours daily on screens. They report elevated loneliness (UCLA-8 mean 1.71), notable depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 mean 1.73), and markedly high anxiety symptoms (GAD-7 mean 2.18). The co-occurrence of higher loneliness, depression, and anxiety suggests a cluster experiencing broad psychological distress, potentially linked to prolonged screen exposure and the pressures associated with advanced education.
